evidence: The user's answers in the displacement-anisotropy interview, 2026-10-24. (3, 4) A preferred direction is reported in three tiers: a finding at sigma >= 3 (unrounded) and >= 1.2x isotropic that holds at the neighbouring resolution (Auto +- 1); a hint at sigma >= 3 under 1.2x, or 2.5-3 sigma; nothing to report below 2.5 sigma. Before, the tool called any peak at >= 3 sigma a preferred direction and the answer check read the same test. Taken as: the neighbouring resolution is nu - 1 (nu + 1 at nu = 1), because the engine's own resolution (recommended_frequency) is the finest tiling whose cells keep at least 12 points each and nu + 1 would go below that floor; a peak holds there when that resolution's own peak test passes (>= 3 sigma, Sidak over its own cells) and the two peak directions, taken as axes, lie within the sum of the two cells' radii (every direction a cell takes lies within its radius of its centre). An axis, not a sense: the map is not antipodally folded, and a two-well site puts its peak on either well from one tiling to the next (dev-jahn-teller's F, 148 degrees apart at nu = 1 and 2); the +u/-u imbalance has its own test. A finding is judged at the engine's resolution only: a candidate at another frequency is a hint. The second call is made only for a candidate (>= 3 sigma, >= 1.2x): on the Demo it takes 0.7 ms (median of 11, the in-process engine; the tool's two calls 1.0 ms against 0.5 ms for a one-call site) and adds 332 characters, 237 tokens by the context guard's conservative estimate, to a finding's result; the description grows by 91 characters. On the Demo: two findings (Ta site 17, 3.15 sigma at 1.95x, holding at nu = 1 at 3.83 sigma; Se site 34, 3.16 sigma, holding at 4.67 sigma), one hint that does not hold (Ta site 25, 4.47 sigma at nu = 2, 2.33 sigma at nu = 1: the tool called it a preferred direction before), five hints at 2.5-3 sigma, 44 sites with nothing to report; every dev split site (17) is a finding. Arm A+ follows the tool's tiers (SWEEP_RULES.directionTier): a split site's peak names its direction only as a finding, else PC1. On the dev set no verdict or score moves (every split site's peak is a finding, and every one's cell is wider than 15 degrees, so A+ took PC1 already); four A+ records' readings now record the tier and the neighbouring resolution (dev-offcentre, dev-jahn-teller, dev-jt-off-centre, dev-octahedral-clusters); arms A and D are identical. (8) An answer that calls a split or flat-topped site disorder when analyze_modulations has not run for its element gets a warning under it: ordered antiphase displacements give a site the same split cloud as random two-site disorder, and only the correlation between cells tells them apart. What the gate did before: its split-site row read the split-site words alone (split site, two-site disorder, random off-centring, +- x A), and any analyze_modulations of the turn met it, whatever the element; a flat-topped site called disordered passed. Now the row also reads a split or flat-topped site called disorder(ed) in one clause (no negation between), and a new check on the answer, disorder, reads list_sites' facts (each site split by the app's rule, isSplitSite, or flat-topped: a negative Mardia kurtosis that is not split) and flags a clause that calls such a site disorder (by number, else by element) when no analyze_modulations of the question tested its element; a ranking ('the most disordered site') and thermal disorder are left. On the answer corpus (ten real answers) neither check raises a finding: no answer says disorder, and the one directions answer denies a direction (Ga, -0.89 sigma: nothing to report). Known answers: directionTiers.test.js (the tiers on their edges, the Demo through the tool, dev-jahn-teller's opposite well), answerChecks.test.js (the tiers and the disorder check, flagged and quiet), verification.test.js (the gate on a flat-topped site), two scripted replays on the Demo and dev-zone-boundary. Approved by the user, 2026-10-24.
